title: Frozen-release inference contract: prompts, response schema, and parameter stability
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Scope: Define and enforce a 'frozen-release' contract for model versions that customers can pin. The contract covers three surfaces: (1) inference input shape and tokenization (prompt formats, special control tokens, function-call schema), (2) inference output schema and deterministic identifiers (structured fields, named outputs, function call payloads), and (3) runtime parameters and behavior guarantees (sampling seeds, stable default sampling params, maximum context behavior, KV cache compatibility and eviction semantics).

Goals: produce an implementable contract and verification tooling so that when a model release is marked as 'frozen-release' customers can rely on no semantic changes in outputs for the certified prompt suite, and performance profiles (latency, throughput, memory/peak GPU) are published alongside the model artifact. The contract must be machine-readable (artifact JSON) and small enough to be validated during onboarding and CI.

Out of scope: model training changes, upstream architecture refactors that are not surfaced to the inference runtime (these are handled by separate onboarding). Also excludes long-term deprecation windows for very old models—this ticket defines the contract and enforcement only.

Enforcement: Add a verification stage to model onboarding that runs: tokenization checksum tests, a golden-prompt regression harness comparing normalized outputs with a deterministic tolerance, parameter stability checks (ensures critical defaults exist and map to documented names), and a performance-profile snapshot recorder. CI must block onboarding if any critical mismatch or performance regression beyond thresholds is detected.

Artifact publishing: For each frozen-release model the onboarding pipeline will publish two artifacts to the model registry: (A) contract.json — declares input schema, allowed parameter names and ranges, function-call map, tokenization fingerprint, KV cache compatibility marker, and deprecation policy; (B) perf-profile.json — measured P50/P95 latency by seq length, tokens/sec, GPU memory delta, and recommended quantization profile. These artifacts should be JSON schemas that can be consumed by Console, SDKs, and Redwood Optimize recommendations.

Rollout plan: 1) Draft contract.json schema and perf-profile schema (this ticket). 2) Implement verification harness in model onboarding pipeline. 3) Pilot with two internal model releases and publish artifacts. 4) Add CI gate for external onboarding requests. 5) Integrate artifact display into Console model details page and expose contract checks in SDK warnings.

Trade-offs and policy decisions: We must balance strictness vs. onboarding velocity. The initial policy will be conservative: any change to output structure (field names, message ordering for structured outputs, or function-call signature) is a breaking change requiring a new frozen-release. Permissible changes: wording inside free-text tokens, micro numeric noise within tolerance, and performance optimizations that don't alter public schema. The team must maintain a documented tolerance table for the golden-prompt comparisons.

Owner: ENG model onboarding team (assignee above). Contact: model-onboarding@redwood.ai for cross-team reviews.

observability: Verification runs must emit metrics to prometheus with labels {model, release_tag, run_id}. Key metrics: contract_verification_pass (0/1), token_checksum_mismatch_count, golden_prompt_regressions_count, perf_profile_delta_p50. Alerts: regression_count > 0 for >3 consecutive runs OR perf_profile_delta_p50 worse than baseline by configured threshold triggers pager to SRE oncall.
notes: We will treat the contract as a first-class artifact: it must be signed by model owner and included in release notes. For third-party models, vendors must supply contract.json and perf-profile.json; onboarding will validate but not modify them. SDKs should surface warnings if client code uses parameters not listed in contract.json.
